text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.69% today, extending a strong two-week rally of 21.5%, as oil prices climbed on Middle East supply fears. Saudi Aramco facilities came under attack and Iran escalated strikes on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about crude oil supply disruptions—exactly the kind of geopolitical tension that benefits refiners who profit from converting crude into products like diesel and gasoline.

The broader tailwind here is a diesel shortage expected to persist into 2027. With diesel inventories already tight and global conflicts disrupting supply chains, refiners like Marathon are positioned to capture premium margins on fuel production. U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near maximum utilization, which means they're already squeezing every barrel they can into products—and those products are commanding higher prices in a constrained market.
